fix: Hoist `parents`, `leaders` and `states` into a scratch struct stored on the tree (e.g. `publish_scratch: PublishScratch` with three collections), and in publish_resolved_leaders do `self.publish_scratch.parents.clear(); self.publish_scratch.leaders.clear(); ...states.clear();`. Pass the scratch fields by `&mut` into collect_publish_state/ensure_published/leader_context (split borrows: take the scratch out with `std::mem::take` and restore it at the end if `&self` borrows conflict). Steady-state frames then allocate nothing.

Allocate nothing per leader: keep a reusable `Vec<LayerId>` in the publish scratch (see the scratch fix on the publish pass), `clear()` it, and build the chain into it. Because ensure_published recurses from inside this fold, take the buffer with `std::mem::take(&mut scratch.chain)` before the fold and put it back afterwards, so a nested call gets its own (empty, non-allocating after warm-up) buffer.

Avoid cloning the whole LayerKind per node per frame. Copy only the small fields each arm needs and borrow nothing across the `&mut self` recursive call, e.g. match on a copied discriminant plus the copied fields: `let Some(layer) = self.layers.get(id.0) else { return; }; match &layer.kind { LayerKind::ClipRect { rect, .. } => { let rect = *rect; ... } ... }` and for the clip-shape arms compute `clip_world_bounds(&self.layers[id.0].kind, world_transform)` before recursing. The clone allocates for the boxed ColorFilter and ShaderMask payloads (`Box<ColorFilter>`, `Box<Brush>`), so every such layer pays a heap allocation each frame.

subtree_generation and subtree_bounds each walk the full subtree of an effect layer, and flatten_layer calls them again for every nested effect, so a nested effect's subtree is re-walked once per enclosing effect per frame. Compute both values in one bottom-up pass over the subtree (or cache `(subtree_generation, subtree_bounds)` on the layer keyed by its `generation` and invalidated when a descendant changes) and reuse them in flatten_layer and write_debug_at.

Use `writeln!(out, "{indent}{id:?} parent={parent:?} {kind}")` (with `use std::fmt::Write as _;`), which removes the intermediate String. Only the debug_tree dump path is affected, so this is a readability/cost nit, not per frame.
